proposals.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, insulating, Li-rich aluminate that is a known chemically compatible interphase with LLZO garnet and is stable against LiCoO2 at 4 V. Its AlO4 framework is a different chemistry from the phosphate, fluoride, silicate and borate coatings tested so far, which all formed La-bearing products at the garnet contact. Al3+ is also a weak reducer toward the garnet, so it should avoid the LaPO4, LaF3 and La2Si2O7 products.
proposals.motivation: Every earlier contact penalty came from La-containing products. The best was Li3PO4 at 0.099 eV/non-Li atom (bin 4), and the phosphate refinements did not improve on it. An aluminate has not been tested, so it is a chemically different family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich phosphate that is insulating and chemically compatible with both LLZO and LiCoO2. It is a well-known protective coating that is reported to resist oxidation near 4 V and to have limited interfacial reactivity with garnet, so it should give a low interfacial penalty.

Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap zirconate that shares Zr and Li-O chemistry with the LLZO garnet, so it should be close to equilibrium with the electrolyte and avoid the La-Zr-P-O decomposition seen for Li3PO4. Its high Li content should also keep it chemically tolerant to LiCoO2 near 4 V, which may give a lower interfacial penalty than Li3PO4 (0.099 eV/atom, bin 4).
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 contact with LLZO gave a reaction penalty of 0.099 eV/non-Li atom (bin 4, not acceptable), so the next choice should be a Li-rich oxide that is more compatible with the garnet's Zr-O framework.

Its fully Li-saturated fluoride anion should be inert toward LLZO and LiCoO2 at 4 V, so it is a plausible low-penalty coating. Earlier oxide and phosphate coatings gave penalties of 0.099 and 0.43 eV/atom, so a halide family is a useful contrast.
